items.headline: The valuation read is being pulled by sentiment
items.detail: The composite sits at the 19th percentile, but the sentiment axis is at 73 while the rest average 25 — the one dimension running hot.
items.framing: Everything is cheap except sentiment, which reads 73/100. That divergence is the story — it's how the exchange-flow build-up first became visible.
items.checkable: Each axis is a percentile of its own history; published weights on the Methods page.

items.detail: Wallet(s) that just crossed the ROI+capital bar by selling a top at profit — a burst means distribution is starting.
items.framing: 2 wallet(s) newly qualified as smart money in 90d (sold a top at ≥5× ROI). Low count = quiet market; a spike is the tell.
items.checkable: First crossing of the ROI+capital bar per wallet, from the sale history.

items.headline: -80% below its all-time high
items.detail: Deepest drawdown on record was -95%; it has made new highs after every prior one so far.
items.framing: Deep drawdowns are the toll — it's paid them before (no recovery promise).
items.note: It's deep and unrecovered NOW; don't imply it always recovers.

items.detail: 0xb744…337d is the biggest net buyer of Project AEON over 30 days — 3.6 ETH ($9,596), well clear of the field.
items.framing: One wallet accumulated 8 AEON (~$9,596) on the market. Show the tornado / the city arcs — anyone can verify it.

items.headline: Holders ~11% underwater — and still not selling
items.detail: MVRV 0.89: price is 11% below the crowd's avg on-chain cost basis ($0.501). Yet 58% of supply is in the longest-held tier — the float isn't moving.
items.framing: Maximum financial pain, minimal capitulation — conviction being tested and, so far, holding.
items.note: Describe the divergence, NOT a bottom call. "Not selling", not "buy".

items.headline: Perp funding above neutral by 33pp
items.detail: Funding 44% APR vs the ~11% neutral baseline — crowd leaning long.
items.framing: Where the derivatives crowd is positioned right now.

items.headline: SPX's MVRV 0.89 = 9th percentile of Bitcoin's history
items.detail: SPX's MVRV of 0.89 sits at the 9th percentile of Bitcoin's entire MVRV history — as cheap as BTC's generational bottoms.
items.framing: MVRV is unitless, so it's comparable: SPX today is at BTC's 9th percentile. BTC was only this cheap at major bottoms.
items.note: A position on BTC's map, not a date-match forecast.

items.headline: -81% below its long-run trend (Fire Sale band)
items.detail: Fair value for its age is $2.4; price sits -81% under it.
items.framing: Where today sits in the long power-law arc.

items.headline: 80% of all-time holders are gone — 92% of today's never sold to zero
items.detail: Of 26,971 wallets that ever held ≥5k SPX, 5,357 remain (80% churned). Yet 92% of CURRENT holders have never once sold to zero — survivorship.
items.framing: Enormous all-time churn, but the survivors are diamond-handed. The honest "who's still here" read.
items.note: Right-censoring: recent cohorts read high. "Gone" = fell below the 5k bar.

items.headline: Smart money still net-selling (-24.4% over 12w)
items.detail: The 11-wallet cohort of proven top-timers (ROI ≥5×, still holding) holds 13.71M SPX. 4w -23.7% · 12w -24.4% · 26w -27.6%.
items.framing: Smart money hasn't started buying yet (-24.4% in 12w). Honest "not the bottom signal yet" read.
items.checkable: A recomputed cohort of wallets with realized ROI ≥5× that still hold ≥50k SPX; net flow of their combined balance.

items.detail: Month-to-date SPX is +0.5% from $0.445 — it flipped green this week.
items.framing: Oct is green at +0% — it just turned green, a good moment for the monthly-returns card.
items.checkable: Current price vs the last close of the prior month.

items.headline: Long-dormant coins are waking up
items.detail: Liveliness 0.613 is 1.5σ up vs its month. Rising = old coins moving (distribution/rotation); falling = holders sitting still (accumulation).
items.framing: Older coins are starting to move — liveliness ticked up. Interesting "the patient money is stirring" angle; not a direction call.
items.checkable: Coin-days-destroyed vs coin-days-stored from the FIFO reconstruction.

items.headline: NUPL -0.12 — capitulation
items.detail: Net unrealised profit/loss is -0.12 (from MVRV 0.89) — the market sits in the capitulation zone.
items.framing: Aggregate holder profitability. Below zero = the crowd is underwater, historically an accumulation zone.
items.note: A position read, not a signal.

items.headline: -1.2σ below its trend vs the alt market
items.detail: SPX ÷ the alt sector (ex-BTC/ETH/stables), detrended, sits 1.2σ below its own trend — cheap vs alts.
items.framing: Relative value vs the whole alt sector — -1.2σ cheap. SPX structurally outperforms alts, so this is deviation from ITS trend, not parity.
items.note: A relative-value position, not a signal.

items.headline: Supply is spreading out of the top 100
items.detail: Top-100 share is 56.2% of holder supply, 1.8σ down vs its month.
items.framing: The largest 100 wallets gave up share this month (56.2%, 1.8σ). Broadening holder base — decentralising.
items.checkable: Top-100 addresses' share of tracked supply, from the transfer history.

items.headline: 172× at this age — vs Ethereum's 74×
items.detail: At the same age since launch (~3yr), SPX6900 is 172× vs Ethereum's 74× at the same point in its life.
items.framing: History rhymes: at this age SPX is 172×, Ethereum was 74×. A same-age comparison, not a forecast.
items.note: Both indexed to their own launch; close-based.

items.headline: 236,432 holders across 3 chains
items.detail: ETH 49,195 · Base 114,034 · Solana 73,203 = 236,432 wallets, +2.7% in ~30d. Base leads on headcount, ETH on value.
items.framing: The real reach: 236,432 wallets across three chains — most people on Base/Solana, most value on ETH.
items.note: Wallets, not people; Base/Solana are bridged.

items.framing: A 65% one-year-plus base — the cohort that held through everything.
items.note: Coin age from the FIFO reconstruction.

items.headline: SOPR 0.999 — coins moving at a loss
items.detail: Spent-output profit ratio is 0.999: coins that moved on-chain realised a loss on average. Sustained <1 = capitulation, >1 = profit-taking.
items.framing: On-chain realised behaviour — loss-realisation (SOPR 0.999).
items.note: Only coins that MOVED; a behaviour read, not a signal.

items.headline: 3.37M SPX left in a day at a loss
items.detail: 2026-10-03: 28 wallets dropped below the 5k bar with 3.37M SPX, 1.9σ above the usual churn — loss-led (capitulation).
items.framing: A loss-led exit wave — the worrying kind: 28 wallets left 3.37M SPX underwater. Say "left/dropped below the bar", not "dumped".
items.checkable: Wallets whose balance fell below the 5k residency bar that day, split by exit vs entry price.
